comment: Power-management policy for the Samsung Galaxy S10+ (SM-G975F, beyond2lte). Read by tools/s10plus/a33/nuxel-power-diag.sh (installed as `nuxel-power-diag` / reachable from the Nuxel Settings power surface). Nothing in this file changes a kernel setting by itself: the tool reads the file, applies only the profile the owner selected, and reports what the running system actually exposes. Battery/charging VALUES are inherently owner-verified and are never claimed from a sysfs read alone.

boot_modes.comment: lpcharge / charger-mode is a DISTINCT boot mode, not a normal boot. A bootloader LPM/charger-mode boot (androidboot.mode=charger) disables sec_ts and other input drivers before userspace runs; there is no userspace workaround on this kernel (CONFIG_KEXEC off, drivers not modular). The correct remedy is an ordinary reboot, never a kernel patch applied from userspace.

charger.remedy: ordinary reboot into a normal boot; no flashing, no kernel change

fuel_gauge.comment: The gauge/charger nodes on this PMIC family are NOT assumed. The tool enumerates /sys/class/power_supply/* and reports the real device names; candidate names below only seed the report. An absent gauge is BLOCKED_KERNEL (no driver bound), not a guessed battery percentage.

charger.comment: Charge control writes are NOT performed by this mission. The tool reports the charging state and whether a writable charge-control node exists; it deliberately does not poke voltage/current limits, because a bad write to a charger register is a hardware risk and cannot be verified without the owner watching the phone.

profiles.comment: Three profiles are defined; exactly one is active at a time and the selection is persisted so a reboot returns to the same profile. Each profile maps to REAL knobs: a cpufreq governor and (where the running kernel exposes it) a cgroup-v2 CPU weight for user.slice. Nothing is claimed about power savings - the profiles are a control surface, and the observed governor/cgroup values are what the tool reports.

adaptive.label: Adaptive
adaptive.summary: Longest runtime. Governor prefers a low-power policy; display and background work are allowed to idle aggressively.

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.summary: Default. Governor preference keeps the interactive feel of the launcher without pinning the big cores.

performance.label: Performance
performance.summary: Highest responsiveness while charging or when plugged in. Governor is pinned to a performance-class policy when the kernel offers one.

power_menu.comment: The menu table itself lives in power-menu.json so the button FSM (bg-03) and this tool read one source. Recovery and Download Mode ENTRIES EXIST but must never be triggered by an automated path; they are wired only to a confirmation the owner performs in person.
